title: Veefin Solutions Ltd - 543931 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Veefin standalone Q1 FY27 revenue rose 128% YoY to Rs 23.14 crore, with EBITDA at Rs 12.83 crore (55.4% margin) and PAT at Rs 6.74 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported standalone revenue of Rs 23.14 crore (up 128% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 12.83 crore at a 55.4% margin, and PAT of Rs 6.74 crore (up 151% YoY). Consolidated revenue was Rs 113.97 crore with PAT of Rs 9.5 crore, which management said reflects the group perimeter rather than margin deterioration. Five new clients were signed, including a six-product win with a GCC digital bank, and the qualified pipeline ended the quarter at about $80 million after $15.27 million converted. The amalgamation is at step five of seven, with the NCLT second motion petition being filed. Management also disclosed Rs 50 crore of short-term debt at roughly 14-15%, secured by promoter share pledges, to bridge working capital.

segments.name: Standalone (Veefin Solutions Ltd, product lens)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 23.14 crore, EBITDA Rs 12.83 crore (55.4%), PAT Rs 6.74 crore; management says this is the purest view of product economics. Revenue split roughly 50-50 domestic and international.

segments.name: Consolidated (statutory perimeter, incl. subsidiaries and group entities)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 113.97 crore, EBITDA Rs 22.4 crore (19.7%), PAT Rs 9.5 crore (8.3%). Management attributes the lower margin to subsidiaries' different business profile, not deterioration.

guidance_outlook: Management says FY27 is the year the platform shifts from building to monetising; amalgamation expected to close within the next quarter to quarter and a half, with NCLT final order as the last substantive step.
Revenue from signed deals to be recognised as implementation fees over roughly 9 months, then licence fees from go-live, and AMC from year 2; all five Q1 contracts are five-year terms.
Services EBITDA margin (about 20%) expected to remain similar over the next 3-5 years, per management.
Half-yearly numbers to show TREDX platform revenue, as payment milestones for signed trade and cash deals fall in later periods.
Management plans to retire the short-term debt (2-3 year tenure) earlier than maturity.
capex_capacity: Management said the capex cycle this year is much lower than last year, but working capital needs remain because revenue is lumpy while spend is roughly constant through the year.
PSB Xchange: 3 lenders live, 7 under integration (about half non-PSU), 22 yet to start; 10 lenders now presented deals (3 live plus 7 in progress).
PSB Xchange limits increased to Rs 5,800 crore from Rs 5,400 crore; cumulative requirements rose to Rs 26,000 crore; 94 corporate deals in the pipeline at some stage.
Management sees an inflection point at 10-12 integrated banks, when inter-bank competition starts.
demand_pricing: Qualified pipeline bridge: opened at $79.62 million, added $20.4 million, converted $15.27 million, and removed about $4.5 million deferred on timelines; closed at $80.13 million.
Pipeline mix: about 70% non-supply-chain finance and about 70% outside India; 26 of 52 tracked deals involve more than one product.

Five new clients signed in Q1, including a six-product win with a large GCC digital bank (LOS, LMS, collections, trade finance, supply chain, limits microservice) and a Middle East non-bank lender taking LOS, LMS and collections; a five-country Africa supply chain and LOS rollout.
Pipeline and deal values are stated as five-year contract value (implementation, licence and AMC fees combined).
Management says Veefin wins on technology architecture but falls short against incumbents with 30-40 year histories.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise debt at 15-16% when equity is cheaper, and why is Rs 50 crore needed if capex is falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited equity market timing, permanent dilution, and the view that the stock price is not attractive. Promoters pledged shares to secure the debt. The debt is for working capital gaps from lumpy revenue, with plans to retire it over two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Is pipeline stalling, given it moved only from Rs 79.62 crore to Rs 80.13 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said $15.27 million was converted and $20.4 million added, replenishing about 25% of the opening pipeline in one quarter. It acknowledged the replenishment should ideally have been slightly lower.

qa_highlights.question: Why are only 3 of 32 lender integrations live?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed delays to lender IT bandwidth and PSU legacy systems, and said non-PSU lenders make up about half of the 7 integrations in progress.

qa_highlights.question: What triggers invocation of the promoter pledge, and what happens if the NCLT approval slips?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pledge is not price-linked. The covenants are EBITDA at most 3x and DSCR at least 1.25, with headroom described as large. Management does not expect NCLT delay; if it slips by months, it is outside company control.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Rs 60 crore subsidiary debts, and did standalone guarantee them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 60 crore sits with subsidiaries Infini and Nityo, and that Veefin (standalone) has provided guarantees for it.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PSB Xchange pipeline Rs 26,000 crore while approvals are Rs 5,800 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said banks set their own pace; the platform surfaces requests to providers but cannot accelerate bank decisions. Competition among banks is expected once 10-12 are integrated.
